items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon announced, limited access
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28, which it calls its strongest model, built for long running agent work and cybersecurity. Access is limited to a small group of cyber defenders for now, and developers do not have it yet. Announced pricing is $2 input and $10 output per million tokens at launch, rising to $4 and $20 later.
items.why: Do not plan around it yet, but learn how long-horizon agents are tested (multi-step plans, prompt injection, overreach) because employers will ask.

items.title: Anthropic adds a 40% government discount on Claude
items.summary: Anthropic expanded its GSA partnership on Oct 27. Government buyers get 40% off Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the Claude API, including state, local and tribal governments.
items.why: Public sector AI roles may grow, so practice building agents with audit logs and clear data handling.

items.title: Liquid AI releases the LFM3 open-weight family
items.summary: Liquid AI released six LFM3 models of about 2B parameters each for text, vision, audio and decision tasks. Weights are on Hugging Face and run with llama.cpp, MLX and vLLM. Speed and benchmark claims are vendor-reported.
items.why: Try a small local model on one of your tasks and compare quality and cost with a hosted API.

items.title: Google DeepMind announces Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4 on Oct 27, a world model for real-time interactive simulation with native audio. It is in limited testing, with Gemini API and AI Studio access for early partners listed as coming soon.
items.why: Low priority for most app engineers. Just know that world models are a new category, and watch for API access.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra added to the OpenAI API
items.summary: OpenAI added GPT-6.1 Terra (gpt-6.1-terra) on Oct 26. Per the changelog it is a fast, efficient model for visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear, natural writing, available in the Responses and Chat Completions APIs. The changelog gives no price or context size.
items.why: Run one of your own computer-use or vision tasks on it and compare cost, speed and accuracy with the model you use now before you switch.

items.title: Decisions API is now generally available
items.summary: OpenAI made the Decisions API generally available on Oct 22 with gpt-6-luna. Per the changelog, a request now takes up to 400 questions (up from 200 in preview), shared input can be cached for prompt-cache discounts, questions can include images, and structured data can be passed with input_json.
items.why: Try it on a batch task such as scoring support tickets: send many questions over one shared context and compare cost and accuracy against separate calls.

items.title: 12-hour prompt caching in the OpenAI API
items.summary: OpenAI added 12-hour prompt caching to the Responses API on Oct 20. Per the changelog, 12-hour cache writes cost 2.5x the normal input token price, so it pays off when the same long prefix is reused hours apart.
items.why: Work out the break-even point: count how many reuses of a long system prompt or tool list it takes for the cheaper cached reads to beat the higher write cost.

items.title: Voxtral 3
items.summary: Mistral released Voxtral 3 on Oct 20, a family of speech to text and text to speech models plus a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit. Mistral lists batch transcription from $0.0035 per minute and voice agent API from $0.04 per minute, and says each turn finishes in under one second.
items.why: Build a small voice agent that chains transcription, a tool call and speech output, and measure latency and cost per minute before you claim it works.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon on Sept 30. Google says it raises the output limit to 1M tokens (up from 64K), and it is rolling out first to trusted cyber defenders, then to paid API customers and Google AI Ultra. Introductory price is $2 input and $10 output per million tokens, rising to $4 and $20 later.
items.why: Test long-output tasks like big code changes and reports on it, and compare cost per finished task against GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 before you pick a model.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol (API name gpt-6.1-sol) at $2 per million input tokens, $0.10 cached input and $10 output. OpenAI says it matches GPT-6 Astra on a coding benchmark at one fifth of the price.
items.why: Rerun your own evals on it and compare cost per task, because price per task now decides which model you ship.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 (API name claude-sonnet-5-5) at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens, with cache reads at $0.20. Anthropic says it is over 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and can cost up to 30% less per task.
items.why: Practice measuring cost per finished task, not only price per token, and use prompt caching to cut your bill.

items.title: OpenAI Agents API with computer use
items.summary: At DevDay OpenAI announced an Agents API with computer use, multi-agent support, tool search and calling, and context compaction on OpenAI-managed infrastructure.
items.why: Build a small agent that uses tools and hands work to a second agent, and know how to test each step.

items.title: MCP Events for plugin automations
items.summary: OpenAI said its plugins now support the MCP Events specification, so a plugin can start an automation when something happens in a connected app. The spec is a community MCP working group draft.
items.why: Learn MCP servers, then read the Events spec so your tools can trigger agents, not only answer them.

items.title: Decisions API (limited preview)
items.summary: OpenAI announced a Decisions API that takes text or images and returns one answer from a fixed list, aimed at classification, routing and agent direction. It is in limited preview, with broad release planned within days.
items.why: Practice using small fixed-answer routing steps inside agents, and compare them with a normal model call in your evals.
